newsitem.title: USA: Mortgage mart goes on prepayment watch after CPI.
newsitem.headline: Mortgage mart goes on prepayment watch after CPI.

text.p: A benign June inflation report sparked a rally in the U.S. Treasury market Wednesday and put the mortage-backed securities (MBS) market on increased alert for signs that U.S. homeowners may soon be looking to refinance their mortgages at lower rates.

Sally Runyon, an analyst at Technical Data, said MBS market participants were keenly eyeing the Treasury's 10-year note rate. "People think 6.10-percent will cause 7.5-percent coupons to be prepayable. So, we are starting to pay attention to that number. Some traders are concerned" about the possibility of a decline to 6.10-percent.
In late trading Wednesday, the 10-year Treasury note was priced to yield 6.19 percent.

Runyon noted that there may be pent-up demand for borrower refinancing. "If rates stay at these levels (for a prolonged period), this will be the first time in 15 months that borrowers can refinance."
Runyon said "There is the possibility that if rates get much lower, 8.0-percent coupons and 8.5-percent coupons originated in 1995 and 1996 may experience prepayments."
Also, said Runyon, Wednesday's session saw some two-way flows in pass-throughs. "There was light activity," she said.

Eight- and 8.5-percent mortgage coupons are widely viewed as refinanceable and market players are watching closely to see if homeowners will prepay their mortgages to take advantage of lower borrowing costs.

But one Midwest portfolio manager shrugged off the lower rate-inspired prepayment fears and said he does not expect much of an immediate effect. If anything, this buysider said he was watching to see how the market perceives the prepayment threat and how it may affect prices.

"I am as concerned about the prepayments as I am about people's reaction to prepayments," the investor said. But, given the rally, he said, "The way we look at the world, the mortgage market is having a decent day."

Treasuries and stocks rallied after the June Consumer Price Index rose 0.1 percent, propelling U.S. Treasuries higher on Wednesday, prompting talk that the 7.5-percent coupon may be on the verge of being prepayable, market sources said.
A New York interest only securities trader reported that the firm tone in U.S. Treasuries had finally affected the derivatives segment of the mortgage-backed securities mart.

"There has been a significant widening in Trust IOs. Strangely, there has been a lot of selling of POs, but at expensive levels," said the trader, conceding that this may, to some degree, be profit taking.

The New York IO trader found that Trust 275 IOs, which have unseasoned 8.0-percent collateral, should be down five-eigths of a point but were off 1-1/8 point. That decline in price may be overdone by as much as a 1/2 point, the trader maintained.
The IO trader said Treasury rates have moved closer to where IO holders were concerned about future prepayments. "I think we could see some real selling if they rally," he said.
Collateral that stands to be affected by prepayments, the trader said, included the 8.0-, 8.5- and 7.5-percent coupons.
POs were trading well, the New York IO trader said.
Earlier this session, the trader said, there were some bid lists with POs.
